fields.statement: Pre-publish audit at 5d28d354 (main plus this branch). SCANNER: gitleaks 8.18.4 with default rules over full history (`gitleaks detect --log-opts=--all`, 887 commits, 6.9s): no leaks found. MANUAL SWEEP of HEAD (git grep over tree, .rhiza/log, .rhiza/rendered incl. Sources and session notes) for password/secret/api key/private key/ghp_/sk-/AKIA/xox tokens, emails, IPs, home paths, private hostnames, phone numbers; and history for deleted .env/.pem/.key/.db/credentials files and blobs over 1 MB: no secrets or credentials found (only hits: a GITHUB_TOKEN secret reference in release.yml, the word 'secret' in scrub docs and a test fixture SECRET-RAW; the two 1 MB blobs are describe-golden.txtar). FINDINGS: (1) docs/rex-upstream/notification-banner.md named the owner's private tailnet HTTPS hostname: FIXED in this commit (now 'a tailnet HTTPS name'); it remains in earlier history. (2) The owner's personal email addresses (two of them): ACCEPTED, no action; they are the git author/committer identity of 913 commits and appear in Actor records in .rhiza/log, so they are public once the repo is, removable only by a history rewrite. (3) A Tailscale CGNAT address and the owner's machine name in three session notes (and their log entries and renders): ACCEPTED as low risk (reachable only inside the owner's tailnet); not edited because .rhiza/log is append-only and renders derive from it. (4) The owner's macOS username in absolute home paths in several log entries, renders and evidence: ACCEPTED, discloses a username only. (5) Other IPs and hosts found (192.168.x test fixture, daemon.home file name, example.com/example.test/invalid addresses) are test fixtures or file names, not private hosts. ONLY A HISTORY REWRITE WOULD REMOVE: the owner emails in every commit's author/committer fields, the tailnet hostname in older versions of notification-banner.md, and findings 3 and 4 in .rhiza/log (append-only) and its history. Recommendation: none of these is a credential; the owner decides whether to publish as is. The owner reads this before flipping visibility.
